observation_summary: The system returned an unexpected time zone ID (e.g., 'Europe/London' instead of 'WET') when resolving certain legacy time zone abbreviations.
reasoning_summary: The bug was caused by an incorrect hardcoded mapping of legacy time zone IDs to specific geographic time zones within the DateTimeZone class. The system was using outdated or incorrect mappings (e.g., mapping 'MET' to 'Asia/Tehran' instead of 'CET'), which led to discrepancies when converting between legacy Java TimeZone objects and Joda-Time DateTimeZone objects. The fix involved updating the internal lookup table to use correct, standard time zone identifiers.
